name: Recipe Book
pitch: Recipes from any site, cleaned up the same way: no ads or life stories, each ingredient shown at the step that uses it, and cooking times that count the waiting.

problem.headline: Recipe sites bury the recipe, then get the time wrong.
problem.text: You scroll past a life story to find the ingredients, scroll back up mid-step to check how much flour, and find out an hour in that "30 minutes" left out the chilling. Recipe Book rewrites every recipe so none of that happens.

stats.label: recipes in the book, from 20+ sites
times per recipe: hands-on, waiting and cooking
minutes for tonkatsu: what the source says vs. how long it really takes

stepsHeadline: From "what should I make?" to dinner

steps.title: Pick a recipe
steps.text: Search by name, ingredient or cuisine, or let "What's cooking today?" suggest a few.

steps.title: Fit it to your kitchen
steps.text: Change the servings or pan size and every amount recalculates. Switch between US and metric.

steps.title: Cook from the steps
steps.text: Each step lists the ingredients that go in at that point. Tap its time to start a timer.

features.title: Honest timing
features.text: Hands-on, waiting and cooking time listed separately, with a note when the source's total comes up short.

features.title: Two views
features.text: Full has the complete instructions. Efficient has one short line per step, for recipes you already know.

features.title: Scaling and pan sizes
features.text: Quantities rescale as real fractions, for any number of servings and the pan you own.

features.title: Step timers
features.text: Run several at once. They survive a reload and chime when they're done.

features.title: Cook mode
features.text: Keeps the screen awake while your hands are covered in flour.

features.title: Add any recipe with AI
features.text: Paste a link, copy the prompt into any AI tool, and paste the result back.
